task: Add five mutating Exchange mailbox operations (send, forward, move, tag, delete) to the ms_exchange toolkit on Graph and EWS transports with outcome-aware errors, a write-specific retry/deadline owner and additive category tagging.

key_reasoning.reason: Touches tools.py (new non-read-only tool classes), tools_vars.py, toolkit.py, client_base.py Protocol, graph_client.py, ews_client.py, plus a new write retry owner and an outcome-aware extension of the errors.py taxonomy (new abstractions). All inside the single ms_exchange package, so not cross-service.

No exact precedent: closest pattern is the EPMCDME-15200 read retry (retry.py call_with_retry) and ExchangeError mapping, which diverge on attempt count, 5xx/timeout classification, Retry-After capping, jitter, deadline-bounded request timeouts and injectable clock/random. Outcome classification (Not applied vs Unknown), non-replayable sends and nested SDK retry surfaces add idempotency risk; permission advice, secret/provider-text hygiene through CodeMieTool._run, and enumerated edge/error AC with no existing parameterized write-test template add a defensive-pattern bump. Delegate/sender semantics on EWS cannot be proven by unit tests.

About 8-10 modified source files (tools, tools_vars, toolkit, client_base, graph_client, ews_client, errors, possibly client_factory) and 1-2 new (write retry owner, possibly write tools module), plus extended per-module tests and a guide update across src, tests and .ai-run/guides directories.

Ticket is detailed (scope table, outcome contracts, retry numbers, 14 AC) but leaves open questions on shared-mailbox sender permission, EWS delegate semantics and whether platform error surfaces must distinguish expired secrets.
